overview: Mahito’s settings tune his passive, summons, and charged body-stretch attacks at different cursed-energy levels.
technicalOverview: Mahito (CP_130) stores seven CharacterUniqueDataTable3 rows. The main row controls passive hits, cursed-energy gain from damage and the CE_2 hold limit; the second row manages his summoned shikigami; three rows are charged CE_2 body-stretch settings chosen by cursed-energy level and one is the Auto version; the last row supplies one Niagara size value for his normal-attack splinters. In plain terms: his kit is about summoning and retiring shikigami, then charging a body-stretch attack that grows toward the target. Runtime code reads these rows by zero-based index through an unchecked accessor, never by the row names shown here.

CP_130.title: Main character row
CP_130.overview: Passive hit counting, cursed-energy gain from damage and the CE_2 button hold limit all live in this base row.

0.label: Cursed-energy gain multiplier
0.simple: How much cursed-energy experience Mahito receives when he is hit.
0.technical: U(0,0)=1. OnDamageReceived first ignores SuperCursedEnergyAttack and SpecialTagCombo damage; for other hits it computes Damage / HitPointMax and, when that ratio is above zero, calls AddCursedEnergyExp with (GetLastLevelThreshold * ratio) * U(0,0). With 1 the calculated experience is unchanged. The reader is the unchecked UniqueRows[0]->FloatValue[0] accessor.

1.label: Passive hit threshold
1.simple: How many hits landed on the same opponent trigger the passive counterattack.
1.technical: U(1,0)=4. AddPassiveHit runs only while CursedEnergyDisabledTimeLeft <= 0 and the receiver PlayerIndex is not 0xFF. It increments HitCounts[PlayerIndex] and compares with the integer threshold: 1 on a finish target, otherwise static_cast<int32>(U(1,0)) = 4. Reaching it removes that count and queues CP_130_PASSIVE (CP_130_PASSIVE_DE on a finish target) as a multi-hit damage request; the hit also refreshes HitCountResetTimer.

2.label: Passive counter reset time
2.simple: How long the hit counter waits after a hit before it clears.
2.technical: U(2,0)=5 is assigned to HitCountResetTimer in AddPassiveHit (seconds). ActionTick subtracts a delta corrected by CustomTimeDilation while input is enabled and clears the whole HitCounts map once the timer is no longer greater than zero (<= 0, inclusive).

3.label: Charge-button hold limit
3.simple: How long the CE_2 button can be held before the charge is treated as released.
3.technical: U(3,0)=5. TCP_130_CursedEnergyAttack_2::IsChargeHeld reads this row-0 value: with the CE_2 key held, a negative value would mean always held; otherwise it returns value > ActionElapsedTime, so at exactly 5 s the charge is no longer held and, once the level-row charge time has passed, Flag159 is set. Auto CE_2 has no IsChargeHeld override. An older verification note writes (3,1); the current reconstructed source reads (3,0).

notes.text: Slots 4-13 of this row have no identified CP_130 consumer in the reconstructed source. The shared camera-request helper reads that range for other characters, but no CP_130 caller of it exists.

CP_130_ATTACKG.title: Summoned-shikigami row
CP_130_ATTACKG.overview: Only the first two values are read: one decides when an out shikigami is pushed down, the other is the lifetime handed to the new summon.

0.label: Out-shikigami limit
0.simple: How many shikigami can be out before Mahito knocks the oldest one down.
0.technical: U(0,1)=4. In CE_1 TickAttack, after the notify it walks Mahito's shikigami array, counts active undefeated ones and remembers the smallest UCN_110_ActionController::Timer. If OutCount >= 4 and a lowest index exists it calls that controller's PushDownActionFromFacing, which zeroes the shikigami's HP and pushes its down action. The comparison is inclusive (>=) and there is no array bounds check.

1.label: Summon lifetime
1.simple: How long a newly summoned shikigami stays out before it drops.
1.technical: U(1,1)=5 is passed as the float argument of PlayUniqueAction(100, value) on the free shikigami. UCN_110_ActionController::UniqueAction stores that float in Timer (seconds); once Timer <= 0 and the shikigami is alive, not attacking and grounded, its action tick pushes the down action. This row is about shikigami control, not an attack-set lookup.

notes.text: The row key says ATTACKG, but CP_130's CE_1 attack set is chosen from the owner action row's Id_AttackSet_CursedEnergy_1 table; these two unique floats only manage summons.

CP_130_ATTACKH_1.title: Charged body-stretch, level 1
CP_130_ATTACKH_1.overview: First charged CE_2 level. It is also the fallback row whenever the cursed-energy level is not 2 or 3.

0.label: Body scale and segment spacing
0.simple: How large the stretching body starts and how far apart its segments are.
0.technical: U(0,2)=1 is read by GetChargeSpawnParams and copied to FieldE0 of the spawned trap record. State 1 grows the trap to FieldE0 over 0.1 s (FieldE0 * clamp(Timer*10,0,1)); each chain segment is spaced FieldE0*400 world units and the tip advances by FieldE0 times the extension-ease delta each update. Per-segment reach is clamp((FieldF8 - segment*FieldE0*400)/(FieldE0*400), 0, 1); visibility and relative scale change only when reach > 0.

1.label: Extension and turn ramp time
1.simple: How long the body takes to finish stretching and to spin up its yaw tracking.
1.technical: U(1,2)=1.5 seconds is the duration of both eases created at spawn (EaseOut, exponent 2, 2 steps): Ease60 interpolates 0 to (number of collision segments - 1)*400 units, while Ease90 interpolates the yaw cap from U(3,2) to U(4,2). The extension state ends when Ease60 reports inactive.

2.label: Hold time at full reach
2.simple: How long the stretched body stays out before it ends.
2.technical: U(2,2)=1 seconds is copied to Record.DurationE8. In state 3 the record adds DeltaTime to its timer and advances to state 4 when TimerF4 >= DurationE8 (inclusive); state 4 calls FinishAction on the trap and removes the record.

3.label: Starting yaw speed
3.simple: Initial turning speed of the stretched body while it follows the target.
3.technical: U(3,2)=20 is the Ease90 start value in degrees per second at the first extension frame. It eases to U(4,2) over U(1,2) seconds. Each tick's yaw step is clamp(Ease90.GetCurrent() * DeltaTime, 0, angle to target), signed by the 2-D cross product, and only runs when the target is valid and the angle gate passes.

4.label: Final yaw speed
4.simple: Maximum yaw tracking speed after the turn ramp completes.
4.technical: U(4,2)=50 degrees per second is the Ease90 target. It limits yaw only; pitch tracking is a separate 10 deg/s step performed inside the same gate.

5.label: Target angle limit
5.simple: How far the target may be off-axis before steering stops.
5.technical: U(5,2)=30 degrees is copied to Record.FieldEC. Steering runs only when the target is valid and either FieldEC < 0 (a no-limit sentinel) or angleDeg(trap forward, direction to target) < FieldEC (strictly less). Here the gate allows steering within 30 degrees.

6.label: Charge completion time
6.simple: How long the charged attack must build before it is ready.
6.technical: U(6,2)=0.3 seconds is returned by GetChargeThreshold for the level that maps to this row (level 1 and other levels -> row 2, level 2 -> row 3, level 3 -> row 4). During the second start the flag is set once ActionElapsedTime >= this value and the CE_2 key is not still held. No bounds check is done on the selected row.

7.label: Spawn offset forward
7.simple: How far in front of the hand bone the trap appears.
7.technical: U(7,2)=70 world units (cm) is the X component of the offset built by GetChargeSpawnParams. It is rotated by the PG_Attack_01 bone transform times Rotator(90,0,-90) and added to that bone's location before spawning.

8.label: Spawn offset sideways
8.simple: Side shift of the trap's spawn point.
8.technical: U(8,2)=0 world units (cm) is the Y component of the offset built by GetChargeSpawnParams. It belongs to the same rotated offset vector; zero here means no sideways shift.

9.label: Spawn offset upward
9.simple: Vertical shift of the trap's spawn point.
9.technical: U(9,2)=0 world units (cm) is the Z component of the offset built by GetChargeSpawnParams. It belongs to the same rotated offset vector; zero here means no vertical shift.

notes.text: GetChargeThreshold begins at Row=2 and only switches for levels 2 and 3, so level 1 and any unexpected level use this row's 0.3 s charge time and spawn values.

CP_130_ATTACKH_AUTO.title: Auto body-stretch
CP_130_ATTACKH_AUTO.overview: Automatic CE_2 version. It uses a shorter stretch, no yaw turn, an unrestricted angle gate and an immediate-ready charge sentinel.

0.label: Body scale and segment spacing
0.simple: How large the stretching body starts and how far apart its segments are.
0.technical: U(0,5)=1 is read by GetChargeSpawnParams and copied to FieldE0 of the spawned trap record. State 1 grows the trap to FieldE0 over 0.1 s (FieldE0 * clamp(Timer*10,0,1)); each chain segment is spaced FieldE0*400 world units and the tip advances by FieldE0 times the extension-ease delta each update. Per-segment reach is clamp((FieldF8 - segment*FieldE0*400)/(FieldE0*400), 0, 1); visibility and relative scale change only when reach > 0.

2.simple: How long the stretched body stays out before it ends.
2.technical: U(2,5)=1 seconds is copied to Record.DurationE8. In state 3 the record adds DeltaTime to its timer and advances to state 4 when TimerF4 >= DurationE8 (inclusive); state 4 calls FinishAction on the trap and removes the record.

3.label: Starting yaw speed
3.simple: Initial turning speed of the stretched body while it follows the target.
3.technical: U(3,5)=0 is the Ease90 start value in degrees per second at the first extension frame. It eases to U(4,5) over U(1,5) seconds. Each tick's yaw step is clamp(Ease90.GetCurrent() * DeltaTime, 0, angle to target), signed by the 2-D cross product, and only runs when the target is valid and the angle gate passes. Here the start and end rates are both 0, so yaw does not turn.

4.label: Final yaw speed
4.simple: Maximum yaw tracking speed after the turn ramp completes.
4.technical: U(4,5)=0 degrees per second is the Ease90 target. It limits yaw only; pitch tracking is a separate 10 deg/s step performed inside the same gate. With 0 here the trap can pitch toward a valid target but never rotate its yaw.

5.label: Target angle limit
5.simple: How far the target may be off-axis before steering stops.
5.technical: U(5,5)=-1 degrees is copied to Record.FieldEC. Steering runs only when the target is valid and either FieldEC < 0 (a no-limit sentinel) or angleDeg(trap forward, direction to target) < FieldEC (strictly less). Here -1 disables the angle limit; with the 0 yaw rates above the rotation is still zero, while the pitch step remains available.

6.label: Charge completion sentinel
6.simple: Whether the automatic attack has to wait before firing.
6.technical: U(6,5)=-1 seconds is returned by the Auto override, which always uses row 5. The Auto action has no IsChargeHeld override (recorded as a false fold), so the shared charge test sees elapsed >= -1 from the first charging frame and sets Flag159 immediately. The negative value is an always-ready sentinel, not a one-second wait.

CP_130_ATTACKB.title: Normal-attack effect value
CP_130_ATTACKB.overview: A single value used as a Niagara parameter on Mahito's normal-attack splinter effects.

0.label: Splinter particle size
0.simple: The size number fed into the normal-attack splinter effects.
0.technical: U(0,6)=250 is read by TCP_130_NormalAttack_1_1 (normal attacks 1_1 and air 1_1). On FX_CP_130_02101 it sets the Niagara float parameter 'SplinterSize' on every component in both the ordinary and the timed effect callbacks, and after that effect finishes it sets the same parameter on every component of the follow-up FX_CP_130_02102. The read and the parameter name are traced; what the particle graph does with 250 is not represented in the source.

notes.text: Other characters pass 6 as the row index to MakeUniqueCameraRequest(2,6), but no CP_130 caller of that helper exists. Only the SplinterSize read above is attributable to this character's row 6.

Mahito's unique data is seven named rows followed by two None entries in CharacterDataTable.Id_CharacterUnique. Nothing looks the rows up by name at runtime: AGameCharacter::GetCharacterUniqueFloatValue performs an unchecked UniqueRows[RowIndex]->FloatValue[ValueIndex] dereference, so row order is what gives these numbers meaning.

Mechanic loop: CE_1 notify spends one stock index and summons or retires CN_110 shikigami; CE_2 spends/fills stock, charges and spawns a TR_040 trap whose segments stretch toward the target; Super shows the domain-expansion gauge. On level change the stock cap becomes 3, 4 or 5, and a raised cap also raises current stock by the same amount.
The battle UI has five stock icons: SetVisibleStockCount reveals up to TransfiguredHumanStockMax and SetStockCount colours the current count, matching the level-driven cap of 3/4/5.

The charged rows' value 3 is a trap yaw speed, not a hold time. The hold time is row 0 value 3 (5 s) for non-Auto CE_2; the older CP_130 verification record writes (3,1) for slot 148, while the current source reads (3,0).

The verification note that groups both CE slot-3 bodies as TR_040_00/TR_040_10 spawners is stale relative to the current source: CE_2's slot 3 is the trap spawner and picks its row by Auto status, whereas CE_1's slot 3 only sets a notify flag and fills stock.

Shared and delegated controllers stay separate: CP_130 has its own action controller and AIType 14 think node, but no CP_130 behavior-controller file, so the base behavior factory applies. Summons run UCN_110_ActionController with ShikigamiUniqueDataTable (not these rows), and TR_040 uses FGameTrapAction_BodyRepel, which never calls the trap's GetUniqueFloat forwarding reader.

Projectile handling is explicitly excluded here: the re-hit bookkeeping in FGameCharacterAction_CP130_NormalAttackBase::OnAttackHit returns early for DamageKind::Projectile, so the trap's extension damage is melee hit bookkeeping rather than a character projectile using separate unique rows.

Zero entries without an identified read are listed as untraced rather than as unused. All owner-unique-float readers (action helper, camera helper, trap/spawner forwarding, AI nodes) were checked for reachable CP_130 call paths first.
